title: Assessment Information
rationale: Retain the NIST security-report comparison as a documentary precedent. It describes an output of assessment, not the assessment activity or a universal enterprise/ecosystem report template.
context_interpretation: R-11 targets the continuing RiskCase; R-12 records basis and R-13/R-17 allow dimensional and score outputs. RX-014 pins context version, while optional method links are completed under the selected analytical task. Revised RiskCase and ArtifactVersion neighbors were reviewed.

title: Assessment Basis
rationale: Clarify the former scoped-absence label as a contrast in definitional scope: generic prov:Entity can describe provenance, but does not define risk-specific assumptions or control conditions. No disjointness, global absence or exact external equivalent is asserted.
context_interpretation: R-12 makes the basis explicit for the assessment information; RK2-022 may identify the control baseline assumed. The documentary specification does not establish that the controls exist or are effective, and different bases cannot be silently pooled.

title: Dimension Assessment Result
rationale: Retain DQV measurement as a pattern analogy. DQV concerns dataset quality; Riskium records a risk-dimension result with its own interpretation dependencies. DQV types and domain restrictions are not imported.
context_interpretation: R-48 identifies one dimension; R-14/R-15 and RX-016 retain optional scale, selected level and scale-version information. C-13/C-18 require compatible interpretation for comparison. The revised ArtifactVersion neighbor does not turn the result itself into a version or a measured real-world quality.

title: Assessment Method Specification
rationale: Retain the reusable procedure/execution distinction from SOSA. A risk assessment method specification adds risk-specific interpretation rules; no SOSA restriction or full method equivalence is adopted.
context_interpretation: R-46/R-50 relate information and scores to a method; R-49 and RK2-018 describe permitted scales/dimensions. The specification retains documentary identity; a separately pinned ArtifactVersion identifies which issued content was used. A procedure description alone is not execution evidence.

title: Assessment Scale
rationale: Retain NIST Table F-2 as an example of an interpreted severity scale. Its security-specific levels and numerical codes are not universal Riskium scales or probabilities and are not adopted as a mandatory scheme.
context_interpretation: RK2-019 declares one dimension, R-16 relates level resources to their scale, and version references qualify interpretation. Equal codes or labels across scales do not license ranking or arithmetic; qualitative values remain possible.

title: Risk Score Result
rationale: Retain metric-qualified output as a DQV pattern analogy without equating dataset quality with risk. A recorded numeric output is neither the RiskCase nor an acceptability decision.
context_interpretation: R-50 requires a score method; R-18 permits zero or many component links for reported scores. C-21 separately requires declared components, a pinned method and adequate inputs for a computed score. C-18 preserves missing data as missing and does not certify a reported number as reproducible.

title: Assessment Scale Level
rationale: Retain the SKOS distinction between an identified vocabulary resource and its lexical label. A level resource is not a value occurrence; this does not prohibit SKOS dual typing in general or adopt an OWL alignment.
context_interpretation: The VocabularyConcept ancestry preserves documentary identity; R-16 assigns one scale and R-15 selects a level for a result. C-13 also requires the selected level to match the scale version and dimension; a matching label alone is insufficient.

title: Assessment Dimension
rationale: Retain the DQV dimension/metric separation as a pattern analogy within its dataset-quality scope. Riskium uses a managed term for a risk-assessment aspect, distinct from the aspect denoted and the judged result.
context_interpretation: The path through ClassificationTerm/VocabularyConcept preserves scheme-qualified identity. R-48, RK2-018 and RK2-019 connect result, method and scale to the dimension. DQV metric requirements are not automatically added to the Riskium profile.

title: Epistemic Status Term
rationale: Retain SKOS vocabulary context for an observed, estimated or projected designation. SKOS does not establish that the designation is epistemically justified or that an estimate was observed.
context_interpretation: R-47 can qualify assessment information with a controlled status. Missing designation remains missing; the status resource, its text and the evidence supporting that status are separate. Retained incomplete/non-disjoint term groups are not newly approved as semantic partitions.

title: Uncertainty Statement
rationale: Retain the annotation body/target pattern for an uncertainty statement, without importing its serialization contract or treating the statement as a probability distribution.
context_interpretation: RX-004 concerns a continuing RiskCase; RK2-012/RK2-013 retain context and its use in assessment information. Revised RiskCase meaning was reviewed. Assumptions and evidential limitations may be qualitative; absence of a probability is not zero uncertainty.

title: Risk Evaluation Outcome
rationale: Retain the distinction between a criteria-based significance/acceptability judgment and a DQV metric result. This is a difference of intended role, not a global disjointness claim between external and local classes.
context_interpretation: RX-011 identifies the case, RX-012 requires assessment information and RX-013 pins a criteria ArtifactVersion. C-25 governs the versioned target. A numeric score alone does not establish acceptability or a treatment decision; revised case and version neighbors were reviewed.
